data.current_phase: Phase A (complete at contract boundary); Phase B (allowed, not completed)
data.requested_phase: inferred: Phase A/B documentation and terminology governance with Phase C/D implication risk detected in c6
data.blocking_reason_if_any: upstream role_citation_verdict is conflict_requires_block with unresolved canonical conflicts; claim set touches target_architecture despite current-state dominant scope (implicit phase promotion risk); c6 implies execution capability before Phase D; c3 touches snapshot boundary contract terminology; c4 requires constitutional document modification while source authority conflicts are unresolved

checked_claims.effective_capability: rename one or more canonical current-state documents in the authoritative document set
checked_claims.reason: Renaming canonical documents is a governance action affecting the entire document authority hierarchy (CLAUDE.md §2.1). Allowed in principle as documentation maintenance, but upstream role_citation_verdict has unresolved source authority conflicts — proceeding while those conflicts are unresolved risks compounding the inconsistency. Must not proceed until citation conflicts are resolved.

Terminology alignment is legitimate maintenance work applicable at any phase. However, with unresolved canonical conflicts upstream and the claim set also touching target architecture, terminology changes carry risk of inadvertently promoting target-state language into current-state descriptions. Requires clean upstream resolution before proceeding.

checked_claims.effective_capability: modify terminology describing the snapshot contract boundary
checked_claims.reason: The snapshot boundary is the core non-negotiable contract (CLAUDE.md §6). Any terminology shift in snapshot boundary language must be traceable to a canonical source and must not weaken contract guarantees. With upstream canonical conflicts unresolved and role_citation_verdict = conflict_requires_block, this claim cannot be safely assessed. Blocked until source authority conflicts are resolved and the proposed terminology is validated against §6 contract requirements.

checked_claims.effective_capability: modify CLAUDE.md, the project constitutional document
checked_claims.reason: CLAUDE.md is the highest-priority interpretive authority (CLAUDE.md preamble). Self-modification of the constitutional document while upstream role_citation_verdict shows unresolved source authority conflicts and canonical_conflict_unresolved=true is explicitly risky — it could entrench or obscure the existing conflict rather than resolving it. Blocked until all upstream canonical conflicts are resolved and the modification is validated against role-matched canonical sources.

checked_claims.effective_capability: modify phase gate terminology or descriptions
checked_claims.reason: Phase gate terminology is governed by SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md (Tier 1 authority) and CLAUDE.md §4. Modifying phase gate language while source authority conflicts are unresolved risks misaligning phase boundary definitions, which could enable implicit phase promotion downstream. Blocked.

checked_claims.effective_capability: introduce or change naming in a decision layer component in a way that implies execution capability
checked_claims.reason: CLAUDE.md §9 and §10 are absolute: no component may simulate or imply execution capability before Phase D. Claims that Layer 3 is production-ready or execution-capable are forbidden unless explicitly proven. A naming change that implies execution capability is a forbidden pattern regardless of implementation state — blocked.

summary.recommended_next_step: Resolve upstream canonical conflicts flagged in role_citation_verdict before any of these claims proceed. Specifically: (1) resolve source_authority_conflict and canonical_conflict_unresolved in role_citation_verdict; (2) re-classify c6 to confirm whether it genuinely implies execution capability or is a naming-only change that can be validated as non-execution; (3) re-run doc-code-sync-check against snapshot boundary terminology before c3 proceeds; (4) constitutional document modification (c4) requires clean upstream state — do not proceed while any canonical conflict is unresolved.
